parts.title: Part 1
parts.transcriptHtml:
Woman: Hello, Andrew, isn't it?

Man: Hi. Yes, that's right. And you must be Mrs. Jones.

Woman: Yes, I am. But please call me Mary. Come in and I'll show you the apartment.

Man: Great. Thanks. I'll just make a few notes as we go around, if you don't mind.

Woman: That's fine. So first, a few general points, Andrew. You probably saw in the advert that the apartment is partly furnished.

Man: That's okay. I've got a bit of furniture myself

Woman: And also, please, {[pets are not permitted in the apartment][1]}.

Man: No problem. I don't have any.

Woman: Well, shall we start in the kitchen? It's through here.

Man: Oh, it's nice and big, isn't it?

Woman: Yes, a good size for one bedroom apartment. It's got everything you'll need. The dishwasher is quite old now, but it's very reliable. {[And I've just replaced the fridge][2]} so that's never been used.

Man: Great. It all looks really good.

Woman: Well, follow me through into the lounge, Andrew. Here we are.

Man: I like the wooden floor boards, but I might want to put down a rug on the floor as well, if that's okay.

Woman: Oh, yes, of course.

Man: I've also got lots of books.

Woman: Well, as a matter of fact, {[I've just arranged for a builder to come and put up a set of shelves on that wall there][3]}. So that'll be convenient for your books.

Man: That'll be great. Then, is that the bedroom through there?

Woman: Yes, that's right. Come through.

Man: There's a nice big wardrobe and the chest of drawers.

Woman: Yes, plenty of storage.

Man: {[But if I wanted a lamp beside my bed, I guess I'd need to provide that myself][4]}.

Woman: {[Yes, you would][4]}.

Man: That's no problem. I've got one that I do.

Woman: And then this is the bathroom. It's only a small space, so there's no bath, just a shower

Man: {[And the water heating, that looks like it's gas, right?][5]}

Woman: Yes. Electricity is more expensive in my view.

Man: You're probably right.

Man: Well, I really like the apartment, Mary, and I'd like to take it, if that's okay with you.

Woman: Yes, absolutely Andrew, I'd be delighted. So why don't we have a look at the tendency form? We're supposed to fill that in together?

Man: Yeah, sure.

Woman: Now I've got a form here. So first of all, I need some of your details. What's your full name Andrew?

Man: It's Andrew Connaught. That's spelt {[C-O-N-N-A-U-G-H-T][6]}.

Woman: Great. Got that. And what's the best way to contact you, Andrew?

Man: Well, you've got my mobile number.

Woman: Yes, I know, but an email address would be good as well, in case I need to send you documents.

Man: Oh, right, I see. Well, my email is andrew171@interglobe.com. Spelt {[I-NT-E-R-G-L-O-B-E][7]}.

Woman: Great. Okay. Thanks. Then I really need an identification number of some sort.

Man: Oh, dear. I haven't got my passport with me.

Woman: The driver's license number will do.

Man: Alright, I've got that. Hang on. It's {[E 738 2991 TP][8]}.

Woman: Right. Good. So, now just a few tendency details. When would you like to move in?

Man: Well, as soon as possible really

Woman: Right. Well, like I mentioned, there's a builder coming that's on the 4 April. So, really, anytime after that's fine.

Man: The 4th is a Friday, isn't it? And that weekend, I'm going away. So how about the {[7 April][9]}?

Woman: Yes, that works well. Now you'll have seen from the advertisement that the rent is $315 per week.

Man: Yes, that's okay.

Woman: And there's also a bond to pay before you move in. It's like a deposit, and you'll get it back at the end of your tenancy.

Man: How much is that

Woman: Well I try to be reasonable, a typical bond for a one bedroom in this part of the city is $500, {[but I only ask for $450][10]}.

Man: Okay, that should be fine.

Woman: Now what I'll do, Andrew, is email you my bank account details, and you can transfer the amount.
